marketplace_description: ismail is an open-source (MIT) music studio that an AI model runs through text. The model writes the song as notes, instrument patches and mix settings, renders it on your machine (the plugin starts the ismail server for you, with uv), and reads every render back as numbers: levels, drum lanes, piano rolls, and comparisons against a reference. It does this because it can't hear. Instruments are built from recorded notes of the real thing, and your own ears decide when a piece is done, through short listening checks. No generative audio model makes the sound.

listing.longDescription:
Make songs, beats and mixes with your model as the producer. ismail is an open-source (MIT) studio where every note, sound and mix setting is editable text, so you can see and change everything the model did.

The skill teaches the model to:
- plan the piece on a one-page Session Sheet before writing notes
- build instruments from recorded notes of the real thing
- read each render back as numbers (levels, drums, chords, structure) and fix what the numbers show
- match a reference recording with scored comparisons, not by feel
- check with you through short listening checks, so your ears make the final call

Needs the ismail server running on your own computer. It installs with Python from the GitHub page, and the skill walks the model through it. It could run wherever the model can run local commands on your computer, such as the Codex app and CLI.
defaultPrompt: Make a 16 bar deep house loop in F minor and render an mp3.
Recreate the drums of this reference clip, then show me how close the match is.
Play me my guitar recording and your rebuilt one without saying which is which.
